iFixit's teardown of the new AirPods 5 has been released, revealing an important but rather small improvement in repairability. Watch the video below.

Repairability score hits an all-time low of just 2/10

Since Apple launched the original AirPods in 2016, iFixit has consistently given them a repairability score of 0/10. From batteries glued down with strong adhesive and soldered connections to housings that are nearly impossible to open and reassemble without damage, AirPods have always been extremely difficult to repair.

However, iFixit notes that with the arrival of the new AirPods 5, Apple has finally taken a small step in the right direction—provided the repair work is carried out by a skilled professional or a bold DIY enthusiast.

In their latest teardown video, iFixit demonstrates that the battery inside each earbud can now be removed and replaced without necessarily destroying the AirPods in the process, earning the AirPods their first repairability score above zero.

Admittedly, the new AirPods 5 only scored 2/10, but that is already two points higher than the combined total of every previous model.

iFixit points out that the left and right batteries are not interchangeable, as the two have reversed electrode polarity and slightly different contact point positions.

That said, that is essentially all there is to the repairability of the AirPods 5. As iFixit shows in the video, further disassembly of the earbuds themselves is still impossible without causing damage, and the same applies to the charging case.

iFixit's teardown also includes their always-fascinating CT scans, giving everyone a detailed look at how Apple has packed the battery, MEMS microphone, H2 chip, and other tiny components extremely densely inside each earbud.
